title: Branches and merging
learningObjectives: Explain branches and merging and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: A branch is a movable reference to a line of development. Developers use branches to isolate work and merge completed changes into another branch. Merge conflicts occur when Git cannot automatically reconcile competing edits to the same area.
understand.whyItMatters: Branches support parallel work and controlled integration. Review and testing should happen before merging changes into a release branch.
understand.analogy: A branch is a separate work lane that can later be joined back into the main route.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The commands create an isolated branch, commit work, return to main, and merge the branch. A real merge may require conflict resolution.

examples.code:
# Example commands:
git switch -c feature/lesson-search
git add .
git commit -m "Add lesson search"
git switch main
git merge feature/lesson-search
examples.explanation: The commands create an isolated branch, commit work, return to main, and merge the branch. A real merge may require conflict resolution.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Create a feature branch, make a change, merge it, and resolve a simple conflict in a practice repository.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
